To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pre modern and the modern forms of knowledge and power are not two mutually exclusive categories but are rather two ends of the same continuum.
the social relations and power relations of pre modern and the modern times, as well as the social relations of production, were different.

(i) the tank irrigation technology in the medieval Karnataka was a product of a specific historical conjuncture and was a part of an integrated system of production, distribution and consumption of agricultural products; (ii) the tank irrigation was not an isolated technology, but it was an integral part of a larger system of production and distribution; (iii) the tank irrigation in the medieval Karnataka had a complex social and political structure and was a part and parcel of the feudal social formation;
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions What is the relationship between knowledge and power in the reproduction of technology? How is this relationship historically and spatially specific? What is the nature of the social space in which the technology is produced and reproduced? How does this space change over time? How does the reproduction of technology relate to the reproduction of social space and social relations? How does the social space in turn relate to the production of knowledge?
how a pre modern technology, in the course of its reproduction in the modern times, is transformed from the pre colonial to colonial and then to the post colonial periods.

the question of how to understand the historical processes through which pre modern knowledge and practices of tank irrigation technology have been transformed in the modern times, and how these transformations were related to the transformations in the social and power relations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the subalterns in this case the tank irrigation communities did not have an unchanging pre modern technology and social organisation but rather they were engaged in the process of making the modern.
the pre modern is neither an unambiguous category nor is it a category of the past.
the subaltern view of history is a situated view that is not only different from, but also superior to the 'view from the outside' or the 'view from above'.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pre modern is a historical category and that its invocation as an alternative to the modern is an expression of a particular political position.
the modernity is not a break from the pre modern but a continuation and a transformation of the pre modern.

the subaltern historical ethnographies of pre modern and the modern technologies and the forms of governance can help us to understand the historical and cultural specificity of the social and power relations in each epoch.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pre modern and the modern are not two mutually exclusive and opposed categories.
the pre modern modern binary is a product of a particular way of looking at things and that the way of seeing like a subalten can be an alternative.
there is no such thing as pre modern knowledge or pre modern technology that can provide a model for the modern world.
